Verified: (a) 4 dealership rows render for July 2026, all with testID `billing-row-<dealership_id>` — no per-user rows. (b) Row headline shows dealership NAME (Ford Bryanston, TEST E2E Motors x2 for two distinct dealerships that happen to share the name, TEST UI Motors) — NOT individual user names. (c) Below the dealership name a sub-line 'N users · Name1, Name2' correctly lists members: Ford Bryanston → '2 users · Zelda Visagie, Johann Linsky'; both TEST E2E Motors rows → '2 users · Alice Alpha, Bob Beta'; TEST UI Motors → '1 user · Alice Alpha' (singular grammar handled). (d) Row totals + counts match backend response (R550/R100/R100/R50). (e) Top totals bar renders: PRICED 10, REPORTS 2, TOTAL DUE R800.00, plus the sub-caption 'Submissions R500.00 · VIN Reports R300.00' — grand total roll-up correct. (f) Clicking a row expands it: Ford Bryanston expansion shows the 'PRICED SUBMISSIONS (5)' section listing all 5 items with reference (FB-000073/74/76/83/89), vehicle, submitted/priced timestamps, R50 fee — plus 'VIN REPORTS ORDERED (2)' section. No regression on expand/collapse; chevron toggles up/down. No React Native red screen, no console errors in either flow. Deprecated packages detected: none new. SafeAreaView issues detected: none.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2979-2986 _dealership_of() correctly falls back to the submitting user's dealership_id when the doc lacks one — this is the migration-safety net. If neither the doc NOR the user has a dealership_id (truly pre-migration legacy), gid becomes 'user:<dealer_id>' and the row is flagged legacy=True at L3081. Clean tri-path.

server.py:3082-3095 For real dealership rows, member_users is rebuilt by scanning all_users where dealership_id == gid — so members[] correctly reflects the *current* dealership roster, including any users that have zero priced submissions this month. This means user_count is the DEALERSHIP roster size, not the number of users who priced this month. Confirm with product: currently for a 2-user dealership where only one user priced, user_count still shows 2. This matches the UI showing 'N users · Name1, Name2' as the dealership team — correct for a shared bill.
server.py:3105-3109 amount_zar = round(submission_amount + report_amount, 2). submission_amount = billable_count * BILLING_FEE_ZAR (fixed R50). Verified numerically for all rows.
server.py:3115 rows sorted by amount_zar desc — a nicer UX than random order.

billing.tsx:301-312 sub-line only rendered when users.length > 0, and slices to first 3 names with a '+N' overflow — good defensive UI. All observed dealerships have <=2 members so overflow not visually exercised but code path is sound.
billing.tsx:273 rowKey correctly falls back to `legacy-<dealer_id>` for legacy rows — matches the review request's testID convention.
billing.tsx:285 shows dealership_name with company_name as a secondary fallback (backend already sends company_name = dealership_name alias, so this is just extra defensive).
